mainTopic: אגדות about מתן תורה: משה and the angels, שטן's search for the תורה, the crowns on the letters, the sin of the עגל, and the meaning of the name סיני.
overview: This amud continues an אגדה from the previous daf. The angels had objected to giving the תורה to humans, and משה shows them that every command in the עשרת הדברות fits human life, not angels. The angels agree, each one gives משה a gift, and even מלאך המות teaches him that קטורת stops a plague. Then רבי יהושע בן לוי tells three more stories. In the first, שטן searches all of creation for the תורה, is sent to משה, and משה humbly refuses credit, so the תורה is called by his name: תורת משה. In the second, משה finds God tying crowns on the letters and learns that he should wish his Master success. In the third, the word בשש is reread as באו שש, explaining how שטן tricked the people into believing משה had died, which led to the עגל. Finally, the גמרא asks why the mountain is called סיני. Two answers are rejected, and the accepted one is that hatred (שנאה) came down on the nations there. This is supported by רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's list of the desert's five names, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: משה challenges the angels: שבת and oaths do not apply to you
steps.stepSummary: משה continues his argument against the angels. He shows that the commands of שבת and false oaths only make sense for humans.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Do you live among nations that worship) idols? Again: what is written in it? 'Remember the Shabbat day to make it holy.' Do you do work, that you need rest? Again: what is written in it? 'Do not take (God's name in vain).' Do you do business with each other?
steps.whatsHappening: We join the story in the middle. משה is going through the commands one by one and asking the angels whether each one could possibly apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The angels had claimed the תורה belongs in heaven. משה turns their claim against them: every command assumes a human life. You cannot rest from work you never do. You will not swear falsely in business if you never do business.
steps.confusionAlert: The first two words, עבודה זרה, end a sentence that began on the previous daf. There משה asked the angels whether they live among idol-worshipping nations, such that they would need the command against עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: (Do you live among nations that serve) idols?
phrases.notes: End of the question begun on 88b

phrases.english: Again: what (else) is written in it?
phrases.notes: משה asks God what else the תורה says

phrases.english: 'Remember the Shabbat day to sanctify it'
Do you (angels) do any work,
that you would need rest?
Again: what (else) is written in it?
'Do not take (God's name in vain)'
Is there business dealing among you?
phrases.notes: Business is where people are tempted to swear falsely

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב: מָה כְּתִיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues משה's argument from the previous daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: The angels' claim that the תורה should stay in heaven.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These commands presuppose human activity (work, business), which angels do not have.

steps.title: משה continues: honoring parents and the moral commands do not fit angels
steps.stepSummary: משה shows that כיבוד אב ואם, and the bans on murder, adultery and theft, also apply only to humans.
steps.simpleTranslation: Again: what is written in it? 'Honor your father and your mother.' Do you have a father and mother? Again: what is written in it? 'Do not murder, do not commit adultery, do not steal.' Is there jealousy among you? Is there an evil inclination among you?
steps.whatsHappening: משה keeps going down the list of commands. He shows that each one only makes sense for people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Angels have no parents, so כיבוד אב ואם cannot apply to them. Murder, adultery and theft come from קנאה and the יצר הרע, which angels lack. This finishes משה's case that the תורה is built for human beings.

keyTerms.meaning: Honor your father and your mother

phrases.english: Again: what (else) is written in it?
'Honor your father and your mother'
Do you have a father and mother?
Again: what (else) is written in it?
'Do not murder,' 'Do not commit adultery,' 'Do not steal.'
Is there jealousy among you?
Is there an evil inclination among you?

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב: מָה כְּתִיב בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of challenges.
steps.kashyaTarget: The angels' claim to the תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The commands assume parents and human desires, which angels do not have.

steps.title: The angels agree with God, proven from a verse
steps.stepSummary: The angels concede at once. A verse in תהלים shows they stopped asking for God's glory to stay in heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately they agreed with the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it says: 'God our Lord, how mighty is Your name (in all the earth),' while 'place Your glory upon the heavens' is not written (here).
steps.whatsHappening: The argument ends: the angels admit משה is right. A פסוק is brought to prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same chapter of תהלים opens with 'place Your glory upon the heavens,' which was the angels' original request. Its last verse praises God's name 'in all the earth' and leaves out the heavens. This shows the angels now agree that the תורה belongs on earth.

keyTerms.meaning: They agreed with Him / admitted to Him

steps.whatToRemember: משה won the argument by showing that the תורה is meant for humans, with their struggles and their physical lives. That is exactly why it belongs on earth and not in heaven.

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד הוֹדוּ לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: Immediately they agreed with the Holy One, Blessed be He,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״ה׳ אֲדֹנֵינוּ מָה אַדִּיר שִׁמְךָ וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'God our Lord, how mighty is Your name (in all the earth)'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ ״תְּנָה הוֹדְךָ עַל הַשָּׁמָיִם״ לָא כְּתִיב.
phrases.english: whereas 'place Your glory upon the heavens' is not written (there).
phrases.notes: That phrase appears in 8:2 but is dropped at the end

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד הוֹדוּ לוֹ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The angels' response to משה's challenges.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The angels agree the תורה should be given to humans.

steps.title: Each angel becomes משה's friend and gives him a gift
steps.stepSummary: Every angel befriends משה and gives him something. This is learned from a verse about taking gifts 'because of man.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Immediately each and every one became his friend and passed him something, as it says: 'You went up on high, you took captives, you took gifts on account of man.' In reward for their calling you 'man,' you took gifts.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new scene. Once the angels agree, they show friendship to משה by giving him gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק is read as 'because they called you אדם.' משה won by stressing that he was human, and for this he received gifts from the angels.

keyTerms.meaning: Gave him something (a secret or gift)

phrases.aramaic: מִיָּד כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ אוֹהֵב
phrases.english: Immediately each and every one became a friend to him
and gave him something,
as it says: 'You ascended on high, you took captives,'
'you took gifts on account of man'
In reward for their calling you 'man,'
you took gifts.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיָּד כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נַעֲשָׂה לוֹ אוֹהֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the angels' agreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each angel gave משה a gift, because he was called אדם.

steps.title: Even מלאך המות gave משה a secret
steps.stepSummary: מלאך המות taught משה that קטורת stops a plague. This is proven because אהרן later used it to stop one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even מלאך המות gave him something, as it says: 'And he put on the incense and atoned for the people,' and it says: 'And he stood between the dead and the living.' If he had not told him, would he have known?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that even מלאך המות gave משה a gift. It proves this from the story of the plague after קרח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במדבר 17, משה tells אהרן to bring קטורת, and the plague stops. The גמרא argues that משה could only have known this secret if מלאך המות himself had revealed it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת מָסַר לוֹ דָּבָר,
phrases.english: Even the Angel of Death gave him something,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וַיִּתֵּן אֶת הַקְּטֹרֶת וַיְכַפֵּר עַל הָעָם״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'And he put on the incense and atoned for the people,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאוֹמֵר: ״וַיַּעֲמֹד בֵּין הַמֵּתִים וּבֵין הַחַיִּים וְגוֹ׳״ —
phrases.english: and it says: 'And he stood between the dead and the living (and the plague stopped)'
If he (the Angel of Death) had not told him,
would he have known?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף מַלְאַךְ הַמָּוֶת מָסַר לוֹ דָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list of angelic gifts to מלאך המות.
steps.raayaObject: That מלאך המות gave משה a secret.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plague story in במדבר 17, where קטורת stopped death.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: שטן asks God where the תורה is
steps.stepSummary: A new story begins. When משה came down with the תורה, שטן asked God where it was, and God said He gave it to the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: When משה came down from before the Holy One, Blessed be He, שטן came and said before Him: Master of the World, where is the תורה? He said to him: I gave it to the earth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second story about the giving of the תורה. This line sets up שטן's search, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: God's answer, 'I gave it to the earth,' is vague on purpose. It sends שטן searching through creation, and that search will show where the תורה truly rests.

keyTerms.meaning: I gave it to the earth

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁיָּרַד מֹשֶׁה מִלִּפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
phrases.english: When Moses came down from before the Holy One, Blessed be He,
Satan came and said before Him:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, תּוֹרָה הֵיכָן הִיא?
phrases.english: Master of the World, where is the Torah?
He said to him: I gave it to the earth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדה by the same speaker, on the same theme of giving the תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שטן asks where the תורה is, and God answers that it was given to the earth.

steps.title: שטן searches the earth, sea and depths, and none has the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The earth, sea and depths each say the תורה is not with them. This is supported by verses in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to the earth and said: Where is the תורה? It said: 'God understands its way.' He went to the sea, and it said: 'It is not with me.' He went to the depths, and they said: 'It is not in me.' As it says: 'The depth said: It is not in me, and the sea said: It is not with me.' 'Destruction and death said: With our ears we heard a rumor of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: שטן goes from place to place in creation. Each place says it does not have the תורה, and the גמרא gives the verses that are the source for their answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that the תורה is not stored in any physical part of the world. Even אבדון and death only 'heard a rumor' of it. It is held by a person, not by nature.

phrases.english: He went to the earth,
and said to it: Where is the Torah?
It said to him: 'God understands its way (and He knows its place).'

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ אֵצֶל יָם, וְאָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵין עִמָּדִי״.
phrases.english: He went to the sea, and it said to him: 'It is not with me.'

phrases.aramaic: הָלַךְ אֵצֶל תְּהוֹם, אָמַר לוֹ: ״אֵין בִּי״.
phrases.english: He went to the depths, and they said to him: 'It is not in me.'
As it says: 'The depth said: It is not in me,'
'and the sea said: It is not with me,'
'Destruction and death said:'
'With our ears we heard a rumor of it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ אֵצֶל אֶרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שטן acts on God's answer by searching creation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No part of nature holds the תורה.

steps.title: שטן returns and God sends him to משה
steps.stepSummary: שטן reports that he cannot find the תורה anywhere. God tells him to go to בן עמרם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came back and said before the Holy One, Blessed be He: Master of the World, I searched the whole earth and did not find it. He said to him: Go to בן עמרם.
steps.whatsHappening: The search has failed, so God reveals where the תורה really is: with משה. This sets up the meeting between שטן and משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier God said 'I gave it to the earth.' Now it becomes clear that this meant it was given to a human being on earth, משה.

phrases.aramaic: חָזַר וְאָמַר לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא:
phrases.english: He returned and said before the Holy One, Blessed be He:

phrases.aramaic: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, חִיפַּשְׂתִּי בְּכׇל הָאָרֶץ
phrases.english: Master of the World, I searched the whole earth
and did not find it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: לֵךְ אֵצֶל בֶּן עַמְרָם.
phrases.english: He said to him: Go to the son of Amram.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְאָמַר לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The result of the failed search.

steps.title: שטן asks משה for the תורה and משה humbly deflects
steps.stepSummary: שטן asks משה where the תורה is. משה answers, 'Who am I that God would give me the תורה?'
steps.simpleTranslation: He went to משה and said to him: The תורה that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave you, where is it? He said to him: And what am I, that the Holy One, Blessed be He, would give me the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: שטן asks משה directly. משה seems to deny that he has the תורה at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's answer sounds like he is denying the facts, which raises a problem: is משה lying? The next step deals with exactly this.

keyTerms.meaning: And what am I? (an expression of humility)

phrases.english: He went to Moses and said to him:

phrases.aramaic: תּוֹרָה שֶׁנָּתַן לְךָ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
phrases.english: The Torah that the Holy One, Blessed be He, gave you —
where is it?
He said to him: And what am I,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנָּתַן לִי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה?
phrases.english: that the Holy One, Blessed be He, would give me the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָלַךְ אֵצֶל מֹשֶׁה אָמַר לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שטן follows God's instruction.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where is the תורה that God gave משה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה humbly says he is not worthy to have been given it.

steps.title: God challenges משה: are you lying?
steps.stepSummary: God asks משה whether he is a liar for denying that he received the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to משה: משה, are you a liar?!
steps.whatsHappening: God objects to משה's answer, since משה really did receive the תורה. This sets up משה's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Humility cannot excuse saying something false. God's question forces משה to explain how his words were not a lie.

keyTerms.meaning: A liar, someone who makes things up

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:
Moses, are you a liar?!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֹשֶׁה, בַּדַּאי אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges משה's answer to שטן.
steps.kashyaTarget: משה's statement that God did not give him the תורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה did receive the תורה, so denying it looks like a falsehood.

steps.title: משה explains: the תורה is God's treasure, and I take no credit
steps.stepSummary: משה explains that the תורה is God's beloved hidden treasure. He was not denying that he received it. He was refusing to take credit for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: Master of the World, You have a hidden treasure that You delight in every day. Shall I take credit for myself?
steps.whatsHappening: משה answers God's challenge. He did not mean to deny the facts. He meant that it is not right for him to claim the תורה as his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'hidden treasure' refers to the תורה, which God delights in every day (משלי 8:30). משה's words were humility, not a lie: he refused to treat God's treasure as a personal achievement.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World,
You have a hidden treasure
that You delight in every day,
phrases.notes: This borrows the wording of משלי 8:30.

phrases.english: shall I take credit for myself?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: משה answers God's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה denied the fact that he received the תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: משה was refusing credit for God's treasure, not denying the facts.

steps.title: Because משה made himself small, the תורה is called by his name
steps.stepSummary: As a reward for his humility, the תורה is named after משה, as the verse says: 'תורת משה עבדי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to משה: Since you made yourself small, it will be called by your name, as it says: 'Remember the תורה of משה My servant.'
steps.whatsHappening: God ends the story by rewarding משה's humility. The very credit משה refused is given to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה would not claim the תורה as his own, so God attached his name to it forever. The פסוק in מלאכי, 'תורת משה,' is the source.

keyTerms.meaning: It will be called by your name

steps.whatToRemember: The תורה is called תורת משה because משה refused to take credit for it. Humility earns lasting honor.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the familiar phrase תורת משה. It also teaches a core idea: the more a person makes himself small before תורה, the more it becomes connected to him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְמֹשֶׁה:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Moses:
Since you made yourself small,
it will be called by your name,
as it says: 'Remember the Torah of Moses My servant.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וּמִיעַטְתָּ עַצְמְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: God's response to משה's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Because of משה's humility, the תורה bears his name.

steps.title: God tying crowns on the letters
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי says that when משה went up to heaven, he found הקדוש ברוך הוא tying crowns onto the letters of the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: When משה went up on high, he found הקדוש ברוך הוא tying crowns onto the letters.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אגדתא from רבי יהושע בן לוי begins. It sets the scene: משה arrives in heaven and sees God decorating the letters with little crowns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the background for the conversation that comes next. The 'crowns' are the small decorative strokes (תגין) on top of some letters in a ספר תורה. The story will turn on how משה acts when he sees this.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
When Moses went up on high,
he found the Holy One, Blessed be He,
tying crowns onto the letters.
phrases.notes: These are the תגין, the small crown-strokes on certain letters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new אגדתא by the same רבי יהושע בן לוי, still about משה in heaven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: משה found God tying crowns on the letters of the תורה.

steps.title: God asks why משה did not greet Him
steps.stepSummary: God asks משה: 'Is there no greeting of שלום in your city?' This is a gentle rebuke for staying silent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: משה, is there no שלום (greeting) in your city?
steps.whatsHappening: God challenges משה for standing there silently without saying hello.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is phrased as a question, but it works as a challenge: 'Don't people in your town greet each other?' It means משה should have said something.

phrases.english: He said to him: Moses,
is there no greeting in your city?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה, אֵין שָׁלוֹם בְּעִירְךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to משה's silence in the scene from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: משה's silence when he saw God
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Normal manners call for a greeting, so silence looks rude.

steps.title: משה: a servant does not greet his master
steps.stepSummary: משה answers that a servant does not start a greeting to his master. Doing so would be disrespectful.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said before Him: Is there a servant who greets his master?
steps.whatsHappening: משה defends his silence. He explains it was out of respect, not rudeness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה reframes his silence as humility. A servant does not speak first to his master as if they were equals.

keyTerms.meaning: is there at all? (introduces a rhetorical question)

phrases.english: He said before Him:
Is there any servant
who gives a greeting to his master?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁנּוֹתֵן שָׁלוֹם לְרַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers God's challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: the silence was respect, not rudeness.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: משה's silence was a failure of manners.
steps.terutzMaskana: A servant does not open a greeting to his master.

steps.title: You should have helped Me, and משה does so
steps.stepSummary: God says משה should at least have wished Him success. משה immediately (מיד) responds with the words of the פסוק 'ועתה יגדל נא כח ה׳ כאשר דברת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: You should have helped Me (by wishing Me success). Right away he said to Him: 'And now, may the power of ה׳ be great, as You have spoken.'
steps.whatsHappening: God accepts that משה should not greet first, but says he should still have offered a blessing of success. The story ends with משה immediately saying exactly that kind of blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point moves from 'greeting' to 'blessing.' A servant may not greet his master, but he can wish him success in his work. The פסוק from במדבר (after the מרגלים) is read as משה finally giving that blessing: 'may Your strength be great.'

keyTerms.meaning: to help Me (by wishing Me success)

steps.whatToRemember: Even a servant who shows respect by staying silent should still wish his master success. משה immediately does this with 'יגדל נא כח ה׳'.
steps.confusionAlert: The words משה says here are taken from a פסוק spoken later, after the מרגלים (במדבר יד:יז). The גמרא says מיד: משה responded at once with a blessing of success. Some explain that when משה later said 'כאשר דברת' ('as You have spoken'), he was referring back to this moment in heaven.

phrases.english: He said to him: You should have helped Me.
Immediately he said to Him:
"And now, may the power of the Lord be great
as You have spoken."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הָיָה לְךָ לְעׇזְרֵנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts משה's answer but adds that he still should have given a blessing.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A servant should wish his master success, and משה did so with 'יגדל נא כח ה׳'.

steps.title: Rereading בושש as 'six hours have come'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'כי בשש משה' (משה was late) as 'באו שש', meaning the sixth hour has arrived.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: What is meant by 'And the people saw that משה was late (בשש)'? Do not read it as בושש, but as באו שש (six have come).
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching opens. It uses an אל תקרי, a rereading of a word in the פסוק about the עגל, and sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of בשש is 'delayed.' Splitting the word into באו שש ('six hours came') points to a specific deadline. The next step explains which deadline.

keyTerms.meaning: what is meant by what is written
do not read (a rereading of a word for a דרשה)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
What is meant by what is written:
"And the people saw that Moses delayed"?
Do not read it "boshesh" (delayed),
but rather "ba'u shesh" (six have come).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching by the same אמורא, now about the עגל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בשש should be read as 'באו שש', meaning the sixth hour arrived.

steps.title: How the שטן confused the people
steps.stepSummary: משה said he would return after forty days, at the start of the sixth hour. The שטן made the world dark and confusing. He told the people that the sixth hour had come and משה was dead, and when they ignored him, he showed them an image of משה's deathbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When משה went up, he told ישראל: At the end of forty days, at the start of the sixth hour, I will come. At the end of forty days, the שטן came and threw the world into confusion. He said to them: Where is your teacher משה? They said: He went up on high. He said: Six (hours) have come. They paid no attention. He said: He died. They paid no attention. He showed them an image of his bed.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the story behind 'באו שש.' It shows, step by step, how the שטן wore down the people's trust in משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rereading now makes sense: the people expected משה at the sixth hour, so 'six have come' meant he was late. The שטן pushed three times: first the time, then the claim of death, then a vision. Only the third one broke them.

phrases.english: When Moses went up on high,
he said to the Jewish people:
At the end of forty days,
at the beginning of the sixth (hour), I will come.
At the end of forty days,
the Satan came and threw the world into confusion.
phrases.notes: He made it dark and stormy, so no one could tell the time.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן: מֹשֶׁה רַבְּכֶם הֵיכָן הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to them: Where is Moses your teacher?
They said to him: He went up on high.
He said to them: Six (hours) have come,
and they paid him no attention.
(He said:) He died. And they paid him no attention.
He showed them an image of his (death) bed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעָלָה מֹשֶׁה לַמָּרוֹם אָמַר לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the rereading 'באו שש' from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שטן used the sixth-hour deadline and a false vision to convince the people that משה was dead.

steps.title: This is why they told אהרן 'this man משה'
steps.stepSummary: The vision of משה's bed explains why the people pointed and said to אהרן, 'כי זה משה האיש', meaning 'this משה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what they said to אהרן: 'For this משה, the man (who brought us up from מצרים, we do not know what became of him).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the story back to the פסוק. The word 'זה' (this) shows they were pointing at something they could see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'זה' normally means pointing at something present. Since משה was not there, the word fits the vision the שטן showed them. This backs up the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is (what is meant by)

steps.whatToRemember: The people did not just get impatient. The שטן tricked them with a false time and a vision of משה's death, and that is what led to the עגל.

phrases.english: And that is what they said to Aaron:
"For this Moses, the man, etc."
phrases.notes: שמות לב:א. The word 'זה' ('this') is like pointing, as if they were looking right at the vision.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמְרִי לֵיהּ לְאַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the פסוק to back up the vision in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: That the people saw an image of משה's death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'זה' in 'כי זה משה האיש'

steps.title: What does the name הר סיני mean?
steps.stepSummary: One of the רבנן asks רב כהנא whether he has heard why the mountain is called סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the רבנן said to רב כהנא: Have you heard what 'הר סיני' means?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens with a question about the meaning of the name סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The questioner wants a meaning that fits the actual sound of the word 'סיני'. This test will be used to judge every answer that follows.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rav Kahana:
Have you heard what "Mount Sinai" means?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרַב כָּהֲנָא: מִי שְׁמִיעַ לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about the giving of the תורה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning behind the name סיני

steps.title: First answer: a mountain of miracles
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says it is the mountain where miracles (נסים) were done for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A mountain on which miracles were done for ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives a first explanation. He links סיני to נסים (miracles).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is based on a similar sound: נס / סיני.

phrases.english: He said to him:
A mountain on which miracles were done for Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַר שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ בּוֹ נִסִּים לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 20.

steps.title: Then it should be called הר ניסאי
steps.stepSummary: The questioner objects: if the name were about miracles, it should be הר ניסאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have been called 'הר ניסאי'!
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is challenged because the name does not match the sound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word for miracles starts with נ, but סיני starts with ס. So the explanation does not fit the actual name.

phrases.english: It should have been called "Mount Nisai"!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הַר נִיסַּאי״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 21.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The name would have had to be ניסאי, not סיני.

steps.title: Second answer: a mountain of good omen
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא switches to a new idea: the mountain became a סימן טוב (good sign) for ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: a mountain that became a good sign for ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא drops the first idea and offers a second one that starts with ס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' shows a full retreat from the first idea. The new idea, סימן, at least begins with the right letter.

phrases.english: Rather:
A mountain that became a good omen for Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הַר שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה סִימָן טוֹב לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer from step 21.

steps.title: Then it should be called הר סימנאי
steps.stepSummary: The questioner objects again: then it should be הר סימנאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It should have been called 'הר סימנאי'!
steps.whatsHappening: The second answer is pushed back the same way as the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name still does not match: סימן has a מ that סיני does not have.

phrases.english: It should have been called "Mount Simanai"!

steps.triggerLanguage: ״הַר סִימָנַאי״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 23.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The name would have had to be סימנאי.

steps.title: The real answer: hatred came down on the nations
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא tells the questioner he should learn אגדה with רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע. He then quotes רב חסדא and רבה בריה דרב הונא: סיני is the mountain from which שנאה (hatred) came down on the nations of the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Why don't you spend time before רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע, who study אגדה? For רב חסדא and רבה בריה דרב הונא both said: What is 'הר סיני'? A mountain from which hatred came down upon the nations of the world.
steps.whatsHappening: Here the final answer is given. סיני comes from שנאה (hatred), because the nations who refused the תורה became hated because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer fits the sound best: סיני is close to שנאה (שין/סין). רב כהנא's remark shows that this was the accepted explanation among the experts in אגדה.
steps.whatToRemember: סיני means the mountain from which שנאה came down on the nations, because they refused the תורה.
steps.confusionAlert: The two earlier answers, נסים and סימן, were both rejected. They are not the conclusion.

phrases.english: He said to him: What is the reason
that you are not found before Rav Pappa
and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua,
who study aggada?

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: For Rav Chisda and Rabba son of Rav Huna
both said:
What is "Mount Sinai"?
A mountain from which hatred descended
upon the nations of the world.
phrases.notes: Because they refused to accept the תורה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא שְׁכִיחַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both answers are rejected, the accepted explanation is given.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: סיני comes from שנאה: hatred came down on the nations from there.

steps.title: Support: the desert has five names, each from an event
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא says the desert has five names, each based on what happened there: צין (commanded), קדש (made holy), קדמות (the ancient תורה was given), and פארן (this passage ends here).
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: It has five names. מדבר צין, because ישראל were commanded there. מדבר קדש, because ישראל were made holy there. מדבר קדמות, because the ancient (תורה) was given there. מדבר פארן...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the 'hatred' explanation with a teaching that every name of this desert comes from an event at מתן תורה. The list continues into the next passage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each name is built from a similar-sounding word that recalls an event there: צין/נצטוו, קדש/נתקדשו, קדמות/קדומה. The fifth name, which comes on the next amud, is מדבר סיני itself, explained the same way: hatred (שנאה) came down on the nations there. That is why the גמרא says 'והיינו': רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's list states outright the explanation that רב חסדא and רבה בריה דרב הונא gave.

keyTerms.meaning: the ancient one (the תורה, which existed before the world)

phrases.aramaic: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And that is what Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina said:
It (the desert) has five names:
The Zin Desert, because Israel was commanded in it;
the Kadesh Desert, because Israel was sanctified in it;
the Kedemot Desert, because the ancient (Torah) was given in it;
the Paran Desert, (because...)
phrases.notes: The explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 25 by showing that the place names come from events at מתן תורה.
steps.raayaObject: That סיני is named for something that happened there (the hatred)
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's list of five names, each based on an event
